speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You've mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for two months; to begin, have you noticed any specific injury or trauma, or did this develop gradually? Additionally, does the pain worsen with activity or rest, and have you noticed any redness or warmth in the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The severity of the pain awakening you at night is concerning for an inflammatory process or infection; are you currently experiencing a fever, chills, or any skin rash elsewhere on your body? Also, has anyone noticed any visible lumps or nodules in or around your knee?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Left_Knee_Clinical_Photo.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work and initial imaging appear normal, which makes a systemic infection less likely despite the severe night pain. To further evaluate the joint fluid and tissue, do you have any visible lumps, nodules, or a specific rash near the knee? Please also tell me if you have a history of gout or are currently taking any medications like allopurinol or leflunomide.

REQUEST TEST: Joint_Aspiration_Left_Knee, Knee_MRI.
REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_MRI_Sagittal_Coronal.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal inflammatory markers make an acute infectious process unlikely, but the severe night pain warrants further investigation into crystal arthropathies or inflammatory arthritis. Do you have a history of gout, psoriasis, or ankylosing spondylitis? Also, is there any morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes?

REQUEST TEST: Synovial_Fluid_Analysis_Left_Knee, Uric_Acid.
REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_MRI_Sagittal_Coronal.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI findings of a "soap bubble" appearance in the distal femur with clear demarcation are highly characteristic of a benign bone tumor, specifically a giant cell tumor of bone. The normal synovial fluid and uric acid levels rule out infection and crystal arthropathies.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone
